text: Section 3(p) of the Patents Act, 1970 excludes from patentability an invention which, in effect, is traditional knowledge or which is an aggregation or duplication of known properties of traditionally known component or components.

Rule 24B of the Patent Rules, as amended in 2024, requires a request for examination to be filed within thirty-one months from the date of priority of the application or the date of filing of the application, whichever is earlier.

The Biological Diversity Act, 2002, as amended in 2023, requires prior approval of the National Biodiversity Authority before obtaining any intellectual property right based on research conducted using biological resources obtained from India.

The Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 defines a patent or proprietary medicine as an Ayurvedic, Siddha or Unani drug manufactured exclusively in accordance with the formula prescribed in the authoritative texts specified in the First Schedule.

Food Safety and Standards (Ayurveda Aahar) Regulations set out labelling and health-claim requirements for foods derived from Ayurvedic ingredients that are marketed as dietary or nutraceutical products rather than as drugs.
act_name: Food Safety and Standards (Ayurveda Aahar) Regulations, 2022

text: Article 27 of the TRIPS Agreement requires member states to make patents available for inventions in all fields of technology, subject to the usual criteria of novelty, inventive step, and industrial applicability.

The Nagoya Protocol to the Convention on Biological Diversity establishes access and benefit-sharing obligations for the utilization of genetic resources and associated traditional knowledge, requiring prior informed consent of the provider country.
act_name: Nagoya Protocol on Access to Genetic Resources and the Fair and Equitable Sharing of Benefits, 2010

text: The WIPO Treaty on Genetic Resources and Associated Traditional Knowledge, adopted in 2024, requires patent applicants to disclose the country of origin of genetic resources and any traditional knowledge used in the claimed invention.

The Patent Cooperation Treaty allows an applicant to file a single international application that has the effect of a national application in each designated contracting state, simplifying the process of seeking patent protection in multiple countries.

The Geographical Indications of Goods (Registration and Protection) Act, 1999 allows a community or association of producers to register a geographical indication for a product, such as a regionally distinctive Ayurvedic preparation, without requiring individual inventorship.
